cve_pair_note: The builder supports cve_pair sources (scanner run on vulnerable commit vs fix commit, labels from fix-diff overlap). Four CVE pairs were probed (launch-editor GHSA-698v, TanStack router GHSA-qx66, astro GHSA-98hj, apostrophe GHSA-7jg5) plus 2,100 npm advisories mined: the scanner's 5 SAST regexes fired on ZERO fix regions — modern framework CVEs are logic bugs, not pattern-shaped bugs. So the Day-8 dataset is expert-labeled (the process generate_sample_data.py itself prescribes: run the SAST engine on sample repos, label each finding manually). Every label below was verified by reading the finding's code context.

label_semantics.0: FALSE_POSITIVE — the scanner fired BUT the code is safe (sanitized / parameterized / validated / test-only, verified by reviewer)
label_semantics.1: REAL — the scanner fired AND the code is actually exploitable (verified by reviewer reading the code)
